title: Vend Pricing Markup and Planogram Terms Printed Against the Vending Services Program
content:
1. Vend prices on a Vending Services Program estate are set from landed product cost at the markup printed against the programme, expressed as a percentage of that cost.
2. Where vend prices rise, the notice given beforehand is the number of calendar days printed against the programme.
3. A change to the machine planogram needs the number of calendar days of notice printed against the programme.
4. The number of planned planogram refreshes in a year is the whole number printed against the programme.

| Programme | Markup applied to landed product cost | Calendar days of notice before vend prices rise | Calendar days of notice to change the planogram | Planned planogram refreshes each year |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Single Machine Snack Service | 52.00 | 30 | 21 | 1 |
| Snack & Cold Beverage Bank | 50.00 | 30 | 21 | 2 |
| Combination Vending Bank | 48.00 | 45 | 14 | 4 |
| Fresh Food Vending Service | 45.00 | 45 | 14 | 6 |
| Campus Vending Network Service | 46.00 | 60 | 21 | 6 |
| Managed Vending & Kiosk Service | 43.00 | 60 | 10 | 12 |

The markup figures are percentages of landed product cost; both notice figures are in calendar days.

### Worked illustration of the markup (hypothetical costs)

Take an item whose landed cost is 2.50 on an estate held at the Combination Vending Bank, where the markup printed against the programme is 48.00 percent. The markup on that item is 1.20, being 48.00 percent of the landed cost, and the vend price is 3.70, being the landed cost together with that markup. The same item on the Managed Vending & Kiosk Service, where the markup is 43.00 percent, carries a markup of 1.075 and vends at 3.575. The landed cost chosen here is illustrative and is not a programme figure.

### The two notice periods distinguished

The two notice figures answer different questions and are not interchangeable. The first is the notice given before vend prices rise, and on the Campus Vending Network Service it is 60 calendar days. The second is the notice needed to change what the machines carry, and on the same programme it is 21 calendar days. The two move independently across the schedule: the Managed Vending & Kiosk Service carries the longest price-rise notice at 60 calendar days and the shortest planogram notice at 10.
